title: Android app, UI and enablement
summary: Compose shell, rule editing, role acquisition, one-tap block
description:
CURRENT STATE: nothing built. Role and notification mechanisms UNVERIFIED — see T002.

The Jetpack Compose app that owns the rules the services consume. Serves R4, R6, R7, R8 and the Android half of R2.

ENABLEMENT (R4): the app must hold ROLE_CALL_SCREENING. Detect continuously — at launch and on resume, not once at onboarding, since the role can be lost. While it is missing, show a blocking screen rather than a rule list implying the app works. Acquisition flow via RoleManager, unverified.

RULE EDITING (R2): same rule model and same F002 core as iOS. Show each rule's expansion count and per-platform verdict even though Android never expands — a user thinks of a rule as one thing, and the UI should not imply it means something different here. Surface equally specific conflicting rules rather than resolving silently.

ONE-TAP BLOCK FROM A RECEIVED CALL (R6) — ANDROID'S ADVANTAGE: a post-call notification or in-app recents entry lets the user block the number that just called, without typing it. This is the most natural way to use the app and it is impossible on iPhone. Mechanism unverified.

BLOCKED-CALL BEHAVIOUR AS A USER CHOICE: if CallScreeningService.CallResponse works as assumed, expose silence-vs-reject, skip call log, and skip notification as settings. Real product value that exists nowhere else — iOS gives no control at all.

AN ACTIVITY LOG IS POSSIBLE HERE: unlike iOS, the app can know it blocked a call. Showing what was filtered is the most-requested thing in this category and Android can deliver it. Design it, and design the iOS screen knowing it cannot have this.

LOCALIZATION (R7): UI strings plus place names with user-language then English then prefix-only fallback.
